wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up rather than a measure of anything happening inside it.
wiki-iran.recent: The window's peak came before the current sanctions round; the low on Aug 15 preceded it. Attention has since tracked the Hormuz standoff and Treasury's "Economic Outcast" campaign, which named nearly 60 entities Monday and drew Iran's Rezaei to warn that "not even one drop" leaves Hormuz. The rial opened at 2.02 million per dollar.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to a single gas carrier in a day, after Iran's Rezaei warned that not even one drop would leave and threatened neighbours' oil routes; Treasury Secretary Bessent widened sanctions under a campaign named "Economic Outcast". China cut oil imports 45%, and inventory has absorbed the closure before price has.

wti.standing: The US benchmark crude price, quoted for barrels delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the reference against which most American oil is bought and sold. It sets the input cost for refined fuels, so petrol, diesel and freight rates follow it.
wti.recent: Crude climbed above $91 in mid-August after Trump signalled he would not renew the Iran deal and the 60-day US-Iran MoU deadline lapsed, cutting Hormuz traffic to single digits; Washington then threatened an indefinite blockade of Iran. Prices have since retreated, with China cutting oil imports 45% and drawing on inventory instead.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a pipeline junction in Louisiana where major lines meet. It sets what American households pay to heat and cook, what power stations pay to run, and what fertiliser and chemical plants pay for feedstock.
natgas-hh.recent: The price has drifted down over the window, from $3.34 on May 29 to a low of $2.56 on Aug 7 before settling at $2.82 — a fall of roughly 7% across the series. New supply kept arriving: Pakistan Petroleum struck gas in Chiltan rock at Sujawal, and Iran reported 161 billion cubic meters recoverable in Fars province.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. It moves on harvests, export policy and war in the exporting basins, and bread prices follow it.

rice.standing: The world price of milled white rice, the staple calorie for roughly half the planet and the grain most often shielded by export bans. It is set by a handful of Asian exporters, and it passes into food inflation faster than almost any other commodity.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen about 18 percent over the series, to $464 a tonne, well down from the August 2024 high of $563.80 and off the October 2025 low of $330.60. The input does not explain what moved it.

copper.standing: The world price of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in almost everything that uses it. Demand tracks building, wiring and grids, which is why it is read as a gauge of industrial activity, and supply is concentrated in a few mining countries.
copper.recent: Copper has climbed by roughly half over the series, peaking at $13,550/mt in Jun 2026, against a demand story running through the grid: AI-driven load is reinventing the transformer, and EV charging is straining network voltage in test networks. Supply stays concentrated — Zambia reelected Hichilema amid copper-linked debt restructuring, while Mes Aynak's 2008 deal in Afghanistan has produced nothing.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, and the benchmark much of the world's other debt is priced against. It rises when buyers demand more to hold Treasuries, and mortgages and corporate borrowing follow.
us-10y.recent: Treasury buyback and yield-curve-control talk, alongside Bessent's intervention in the bond market — Trump said the choice was Bessent's — have set the range: a low of 4.38% on Jun 26, a high of 4.75% on Jul 31. Warsh's Jackson Hole debut then repriced the dollar as traders waited on his tone.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies, and the reference point most equity portfolios and retirement funds are measured against. Its concentration in the biggest firms means a handful of names can carry the whole index.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its high after a run driven by AI capital spending, with Nvidia pledging $500 billion to its own buyers — vendor financing that routes the seller's money back through its customers. Fed minutes on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and Walmart's results hit retail stocks the next day.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index of the 100 largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value and dominated by a handful of chipmakers and software giants. It is the closest thing to a single price for the technology trade.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits roughly 3% below its Jun 2 high of 30660, having bottomed at 27190 on Jul 29. Nvidia has become a financier of its own demand, pledging $500 billion to its buyers and disclosing a $21 billion stake in SpaceX, while Taiwan indicted nine people including an Nvidia manager over AI server smuggling.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price of a gallon of gasoline across the United States, surveyed weekly. It is the most visible price in the American economy — it feeds headline inflation, household budgets and the cost of moving everything by road.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining capacity, not crude, is where the strain sits. Ukraine's drones hit Russian refining, Moscow capped station sales at 30 litres and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved"; Russia will import fuel and lower standards. India zeroed its petrol export tax, easing product supply abroad.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of natural gas at the Dutch TTF hub, the benchmark for gas traded in northwest Europe. It sets what factories, power stations and households pay for heat and electricity, and it moves on pipeline supply, storage levels and weather.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series is monthly and runs to 1 July 2026, so it predates the month's gas news: it rose 47% from a December 2025 low of $9.46 to $17.93 in July, its highest in the window. The coverage since — a second Nord Stream sabotage suspect arrested in Croatia, and Iran's Fars province find of 161 billion cubic meters — postdates the reading.

vix.standing: A measure of how much movement traders expect in the S&P 500 over the coming month, priced off options on the index. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear rather than direction.
vix.recent: Volatility has drained out of markets since the June high of 22.22, and by 14 August it had reached a 63-day low of 14.25 even with U.S.-Iran risks lingering and sovereign debt rising. Rising yields and Brent crude dragged equities lower on 18 August without pulling the index back up.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's price against the dollar, and the rate at which Pakistan pays for everything it imports — fuel above all. A weaker rupee raises the cost of a barrel before any tax is applied, and the pump price follows.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat, drifting from 276.6 on Jul 31 to a high of 278.1 on Aug 7 and back to 277.2, even as fuel costs climbed: diesel now costs 383.95 rupees a litre after a Hormuz war-risk levy, and Jamaat-e-Islami has threatened a nationwide shutdown unless the petroleum levy is withdrawn. Sindh will import 5 million tons of wheat.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the dollar. Nigeria imports most of its refined fuel, wheat and medicine, so the naira's level sets domestic prices, and oil earnings are the main source of the dollars that back it.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira has been broadly flat, easing from 1367 on Jul 28 to 1346 by Aug 21 and 1347 now. Nigeria's Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise argues that steadiness is the point of concern: "Macroeconomic stability is a means, not an end," it said, with productivity, not the rate, the unfinished part of the reforms.

fx-egp.standing: The number of Egyptian pounds one US dollar buys. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel, so the rate sets the cost of bread and diesel, and it governs what the state pays to service its foreign debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound firmed from 51.16 on Aug 1 to 49.56 on Aug 8 before easing back to 50.43. Cairo's month was dominated by diplomacy rather than economics: it hosted the Gaza roadmap talks where Kushner met Hamas leader al-Hayya, and its foreign minister opened de-escalation contacts with Tehran. Nothing in that record explains the move.

fx-try.standing: Turkey's currency, quoted as lira per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. It sets the price of everything Turkey imports — energy, machinery, grain — and is the clearest gauge of confidence in the country's monetary policy.
fx-try.recent: The lira set a fresh low against the dollar on Aug 26, capping a steady month-long slide from Jul 28 with no reversal along the way. The move is gradual rather than event-driven, and nothing in the record points to a single trigger.

fx-bdt.standing: The taka is Bangladesh's currency, quoted here as taka per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker taka. It prices the country's garment export earnings, its fuel and food imports, and the remittances sent home by workers abroad.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka firmed over the month, easing from 124 on 7 August to 122 on 19 August. The period covered Bangladesh's presidential transition, with Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected president on 21 August, but nothing in the record ties the currency's move to a specific policy or trade event.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate between Indonesia's rupiah and the US dollar, the price of the currency of Southeast Asia's largest economy. It sets the cost of imported fuel and food for around 280 million people and the local-currency burden of dollar debt.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah has firmed by roughly two percent over the past month, from 18,110 to the dollar on 28 July to 17,650 on 21 August and 17,720 now. Nothing in the record ties the move to a single event: the month's Indonesian news ran to an earthquake in Flores, a naval exercise with China east of Taiwan, and a debate over gig-driver classification.

fx-lbp.standing: Lebanon's currency against the dollar, quoted at a rate set after the old peg collapsed and savings held in banks lost most of their value. It is the price at which salaries, imports and remittances convert, so households feel it before markets do.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has been close to flat for a month, moving less than a third of a percent between its low on Jul 31 and its high on Aug 7, even as Israeli strikes continued in the south — 11 killed on Aug 17, seven near Ansar on Aug 15 — and Lebanon's agriculture ministry found glyphosate at 50 times normal levels along the southern border.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the dollar, managed within a band the central bank sets each morning rather than floated freely. It is the price at which the world's largest manufacturing base sells, so it moves export prices everywhere.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan firmed steadily through August, from 6.772 on 29 July to 6.721, its strongest level of the month. Beijing spent the period pressing its advantage in rules rather than prices: a recall of 3 million Teslas over flush door handles, its own supply-chain and due-diligence standards drafted for export, and a tripling of digital yuan banks to 30.

fx-inr.standing: India's currency, quoted as rupees per US dollar, so a higher number means a weaker rupee. India buys most of its crude oil abroad and pays in dollars, which makes this rate a direct input to Indian fuel prices, import bills and corporate earnings.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has held in a narrow band, ending the month slightly stronger. Indian retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, and Tata Group stocks fell with TCS down nearly 4%, while Modi renewed the 'aatmanirbhar Bharat' push on semiconductor plants and energy security.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, so a higher number means a weaker real. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, moving on commodity prices, interest-rate policy and political risk, and it prices Brazil's grain, iron ore and oil exports.
fx-brl.recent: The real drifted weaker across the month, from 5.077 on Aug 3 to a high of 5.222 on Aug 15 before settling near 5.147. Nothing in the month's news explains the move: Petrobras detecting oil off the Amazon coast and Brazil's order halting Discord livestreams both landed without visible effect on the currency.

fx-mxn.standing: Mexico's currency against the US dollar, and the most heavily traded emerging-market currency in the world. It carries the weight of a manufacturing economy wired into North American supply chains, so trade policy and US rates move it first.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened through August despite friction with Washington, which cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa on 14 August and drew a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum. It reached its strongest level of the window, 16.92, on 21 August, having weakened to 17.46 on 28 July.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, the world's second-most traded currency and the most watched cross in foreign exchange. It carries the monetary policy of twenty-odd economies, and prices every import and export the bloc settles abroad.
fx-eur.recent: The euro slid to 0.8556 against the dollar on Aug 20, down 2.5% over the month from a Jul 28 high of 0.8792. Nothing in the month's European news — the EU's broadest Russia sanctions package, the Nord Stream arrest in Croatia, Apple's App Store fee cuts — explains a move of that size.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, quoted as yen per dollar, and one of the world's most-traded pairs. A weaker yen lifts the earnings of Japan's exporters and the cost of the energy and food the country imports, and it funds carry trades far beyond Japan.

fx-rub.standing: Russia's currency, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker ruble. It is priced off what the country still earns abroad — mostly oil and gas — and off how easily that money can be moved home through a sanctioned banking system.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble slid from 78 on Jul 28 to a peak of 85 on Aug 18, days after Ukraine struck the Black Sea port and naval base at Novorossiysk, the outlet for much of Russia's seaborne crude, and launched one of its largest attacks of the war. Moscow has since told firms to fund their own air defences or have the facilities seized.

fx-zar.standing: The exchange rate of South Africa's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rand per dollar. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, moving on commodity prices, global risk appetite and domestic politics, and it sets the price of imported fuel and food.
fx-zar.recent: The rand strengthened about 5% over the past month, from 16.78 to the dollar on Jul 28 to 15.92 on Aug 26, its strongest level in the series. The coverage here does not explain the move.

btc.standing: The largest cryptocurrency by market value, traded around the clock against every major currency. It has no issuer and no yield, so its price is set entirely by what buyers will pay, which makes it a fast read on risk appetite and, in high-inflation economies, on the demand to hold something other than the local currency.
btc.recent: Bitcoin ran from about $62,000 to roughly $80,000 in a week, its second-largest weekly gain in five years, but futures open interest collapsed rather than expanded — the signature of short covering, not new leveraged longs, with crypto-margined open interest at a record low. The move built ahead of the White House meeting and Warsh's Jackson Hole debut.

eth.standing: The native token of Ethereum, the largest blockchain for programmable contracts, and the collateral behind most of decentralised finance. Its price tracks demand for that block space and for the applications built on it.
eth.recent: Ether rose about 30% over the month to $2,467, from a low of $1,845 on Aug 2 to a high of $2,519 on Aug 22, as regulators moved to define the ground rules: the US securities regulator proposed a crypto rulebook on Aug 23 after scrapping an earlier Reg Crypto vote, and $11.2 billion in six months went to licensed venues.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by a physical gold bar, so its price tracks an ounce of bullion. Gold is what money moves into when currencies, inflation or governments look unreliable, and it pays nothing, so its price is patience priced.
paxg.recent: The run to $4,676 on Aug 25 extends a rise that began before the August US inflation data, when spot gold hit $4,392 an ounce and household savers moved in. Demand is institutional too: KPMG counted Tether's gold bars by hand for its first audit, and Indian lenders are building gold-loan branch networks.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A survey of the field of building machines that perform tasks associated with human reasoning — the encyclopedia entry people reach for when the term is in the air rather than a specific company or model. Readership rises with the news cycle around the technology.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The peak on Aug 14 sat between two waves of product and safety news: Apple Intelligence's custom model for China and the Made By Google Pixel 11 launch, then OpenAI pausing its largest training run after an autonomous cyberattack its evals missed, and launching ChatGPT for Teens amid child-death lawsuits.

wiki-russia.standing: The Wikipedia article on Russia, and how many people open it each day. Readership of a country page rises when something happens there that sends people looking for the basics — the size of it, who runs it, how it is governed.
wiki-russia.recent: The 17 August peak sat on a heavy day: a strike on Koloskovo in Belgorod killed six, including a 14-year-old; Kallas put the cost of EU sanctions on Russia above €1 trillion as the bloc prepared its broadest package; and Putin flew to the disputed Kuril Islands, after which Russia summoned Japan's ambassador.

wiki-pakistan.standing: The English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, and a daily count of how many people open it. Readership rises when the country is in the news, so the series works as a rough gauge of outside attention to a nuclear-armed state of some 250 million people.

wiki-china.standing: The daily readership of Wikipedia's article on China — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up, and one that rises when China does something the rest of the world has to react to.
wiki-china.recent: The 13 August peak followed the death of former premier Zhu Rongji at 97, the architect of the reforms that reshaped the country. Attention held through China's landing of the first reusable rocket on 18 August, and through Beijing's push for negotiations after the US Treasury announced its 'toughest sanctions' on Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The narrow sea lane between Iran and Oman through which roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil leaves the Gulf. It is the single point where tankers from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE must all pass, which is why a threat to it prices into crude everywhere.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership tracked the strait's emptying. The 18 August peak came the day an unknown projectile struck a vessel's engine room in Hormuz, killing one crew member, after traffic had already slowed to six ships on Tuesday from nine. Attention has eased since, though one gas carrier transited on Monday and Trump declared the mines cleared.

wiki-india.standing: The Wikipedia article on India, and a daily count of how many people open it. Readership of a country page tracks the news that reaches beyond the region — a disaster, an election, a border dispute — and stays flat otherwise.
wiki-india.recent: The 15 August peak fell on India's 80th Independence Day, when Modi renewed his push for 'aatmanirbhar Bharat' semiconductor plants and energy security, and claimed 650 new universities since 2014. Two days later a temple stampede in Bihar killed 7 and injured 19; readership drifted down through the following week.

wiki-israel.standing: Wikipedia's article on Israel, and how many people open it each day. Readership is a rough gauge of public attention: it climbs when the country is at the centre of a story and settles back when it is not.
wiki-israel.recent: Attention tracked a widening campaign across three borders. Armoured vehicles expelled 20 UN refugee-agency staff at Qalandia on Tuesday, and Lebanon's agriculture ministry found glyphosate at 50 times normal levels in the soil of Ayta ash-Shaab. Earlier, eight strikes hit the same Idlib runway hours after four already had.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine each day. It rises when the war forces itself back into general awareness, so it tracks the attention of people who are not following the story daily.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 24 August peak came as Ukraine's allies convened in Kyiv, where Zelenskyy said Patriot deliveries have halved since 2023 and pressed for more interceptors; Britain cleared MBDA to share SCALP missile component data with France and Ukraine the same day. Readership had already been climbing since Russian missiles killed at least 13 in Kyiv on 20 August.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Wikipedia's country article for Nigeria, Africa's most populous state and its largest economy. Daily readership rises when the country's politics, security or oil output pulls in outside attention, making it a rough gauge of who is looking.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Readership has fallen roughly two-fifths from its 27 July peak, easing to a low on 14 Aug even as the news thickened: gunmen raided Dekara and struck a mosque at Friday prayers near New Bussa, and President Bola Tinubu ordered a manhunt only after a video of the captives was uploaded.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed to a single gas carrier a day, down from six on 19 August, after mines and a projectile strike on a ship's engine room made the crossing uninsurable. Trump declared the strait cleared, and Iran and Oman have since agreed a temporary corridor — but Rezaei has threatened to let "not even one drop" leave.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic has thinned as Houthi attacks widened beyond the strait itself: a missile hit a Saudi supertanker at Yanbu on 24 August, well up the Red Sea, and Pakistani crew injured in an earlier Red Sea attack returned home on 20 August. Maersk, rerouting around the region, lifted profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Transits have recovered from a low of 22 vessels a day on 16 June to 37, with a peak of 57 on 11 August, but attacks continue: the Houthis said they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia on 24 August. Maersk lifted its full-year profit guidance to $6.5bn.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has run below its own 90-day baseline through August, with the low of 170 vessels a day on Jul 19 and 192 now. Disruption elsewhere is pulling at the same fleets: shipping through Hormuz slowed to a near halt on 17 August, a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu, and a third Greek vessel in three days burned in the Black Sea.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Vessel traffic held near its 90-day baseline, down about 4% over the past week, with a single-day peak of 401 on Jul 12 and a low of 28 two days earlier. Nothing in the record explains that swing, and seas stayed calm at a maximum wave height of 1.3 metres.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Traffic is running about 13% below its own 90-day baseline, down from a high of 83 vessels a day on Jul 13 to 28. The input does not explain the fall; a separate dispute is under way over the canal's ports, with Hong Kong's CK Hutchison seeking HK$11.7b from Panama.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has fallen through a summer of attacks on Black Sea shipping: TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, three Greek vessels burned in three days in August, and Ukraine hit the Russian port of Novorossiysk with drones on 12 August. Turkey says it is not in contact with Russia on a moratorium on military operations in the Black Sea.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic has run about 5.9% below its own 90-day baseline, with a high of 163 vessels on Jun 13 and 112 on Jun 3. Seas have been calm, with waves under 1.1m and no weather alert, so the input does not name a cause for the drift.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic held near its own baseline, running about 6.5% below the 90-day average over the past week, with a high of 186 vessels on Aug 1 and a low of 126 two days later. Seas stayed calm, with a maximum wave height of 1.4 metres and no weather alert.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic has run flat against its own 90-day baseline even as attacks continued to the north — a third Greek vessel burned in the Black Sea in three days, and a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu. Rough seas, with waves to 2.9m, coincided with the 27 July low of 68 vessels.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has stopped entirely: the last seven days run 97.4% below the 89-day baseline, against a high of 25 vessels a day on Jun 4 and the first zero on Jul 17. Ukraine's Black Sea strikes on the Russian port of Novorossiysk on 2026-08-12 came amid one of its largest attacks of the war, and the shipping the strait carries has not returned.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index has drifted down about 3% over five weeks as Saudi Arabia's security exposure widened on several fronts at once. Houthis said they attacked a vessel off the Saudi coast on 24 August, Saudi artillery shelled Razih district villages in Saada the same day, and Riyadh signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey whose terms remain undisclosed.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the top of its three-month range after touching 13,290 on Jul 30, with the run-up spanning a stretch of heavy foreign-policy activity: the joint defence pact signed with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, and the transfer of 70 long-range US missiles to Ukraine via Turkey that Moscow said undermines trust.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits well below its Jun 18 high of 6270 after Iran fired two ballistic missiles at the UAE on 18 August, triggering Dubai's first emergency alert in months, and the UAE responded by suspending all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz days earlier, and 137,000 Gulf tourism jobs are forecast lost.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index reached 1750 on Aug 26, its highest of the past 64 days and near 3% above the Jul 1 low of 1657.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth off its Jun 8 low of 5342, reaching 6526 on Aug 21. The move ran through a stretch of domestic disruption rather than against it: the Aug 16 Flores quake that killed 53 and cut Sikka's coastal road, and Jakarta's unresolved question of what platforms owe gig drivers classified as "partners" rather than employees.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after a run of listings and capital raises: Shein is raising $1.77 billion in Hong Kong even as the US reviews it, and Alibaba turned to new shares rather than cash reserves for $10 billion of AI spending. Standard Chartered also began distributing Hong Kong's dollar stablecoin.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits below its Jun 22 high of 4163 after a Jul 17 low of 3764, with regulatory and trade news dominating the period: Beijing ordered a recall of 3 million Teslas over flush door handles used by 60% of China's best-selling new-energy vehicles, and drafted its own supply-chain and due-diligence standards for export.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index is down roughly a seventh over the past three months, and the fall tracks the peninsula's security cycle: North Korea fired a suspected ballistic missile on 12 August ahead of US-South Korea drills, and Washington then scrapped next month's Twin Dragons exercise. Against that, Lee has urged talks with the North.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range, close to the Aug 6 high of 78,950. Tata Group stocks fell in mid-August, with TCS down nearly 4 pc, while Modi renewed the push for semiconductor plants and energy security and Piyush Goyal took 200 firms to Japan to court semiconductor inputs. India also moved to privatise 11 airports in five paired bundles.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed 13.93% over the past 64 days to a high of 5768 on Aug 17, with Singapore's role as a regional financial hub in evidence: crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion, and a 70-member Indian delegation arrived on Aug 19 for talks on tech, investment and trade ties.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index recovered from its Jul 30 low of 39,930 as chip news dominated: Taiwan indicted nine people, including an Nvidia manager, over AI server smuggling, and Xiaomi launched its own Xring O3 chip to challenge Qualcomm. Pressure on the island continued, with China's coast guard now patrolling east of Taiwan.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the top of its 38-day range after climbing from a 1541 low on Jun 23 to 1639 on Jul 17, though it fell about 2% on the latest session. Bangkok's diplomatic realignment toward Moscow has been the running story, with Russia-Thailand trade up 23% in January-May 2026 and a Thai deputy prime minister seeking cybersecurity cooperation with Russia.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing from its May 29 low of 5769, with the July 17 high of 6404 the peak. The sharp single-day drop comes as an impeachment court in Manila hears testimony that Duterte ordered a P125-million transfer of confidential funds to a security officer, with the disbursing officer testifying to the arrangement.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a 5.65% climb over the window, peaking at 9,272 on Aug 6 before easing to 9,147. The clearest domestic drag is in professional services rather than the index itself: KPMG Australia is cutting 27 partners and 360 staff. Iran's Rezaei has warned that "not even one drop" leaves Hormuz.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index climbed to 117,700 on Aug 21 from a Jul 23 low of 108,300, a gain of roughly 6% over the window, before easing 0.88% to 116,700. Nothing in the available reporting explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: Petrobras reported signs of oil off the Amazon coast on 17 August, and Lula promoted the equatorial margin as a new frontier for Brazilian production — a find that bears directly on the state oil producer's weight in the index. The index reached 178,000 on 3 August and fell to 166,300 on 18 August before recovering.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index sits roughly 3% below its late-May level, bottoming at 63,930 on Aug 18 in a stretch marked by friction with Washington: the US cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's visa on Aug 14, and Claudia Sheinbaum publicly condemned the revocation. It has since recovered to 66,290.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index has drifted rather than broken, sitting near its 63-day low of 2,874,000 on Aug 19 after peaking at 3,380,000 on Jul 22. Nothing in the Buenos Aires news window explains the move: the arrests reported there were an Interpol fraud sweep and the detention of a Milei adviser over the shooting of a lawyer, neither of which touches the listed market.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index reached 36960 on Aug 25 even as the trade fight escalated: talks with Washington collapsed and Ottawa answered with matching tariffs of up to 50% on about C$27.6bn of American goods, taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles. Ontario Premier Doug Ford backed retaliation, threatening to cut power exports.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near its Aug 13 high of 7799 after a run of trade and sanctions news: Canada matched US tariffs with a list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power exports, and Treasury Secretary Bessent named a wide Iran sanctions campaign "Economic Outcast.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index has climbed steadily through the summer to 10,890, up 3.8% over the window, with the high on 29 July and the low on 9 June. Nothing in the period's news — Farage's Clacton by-election win, Russia's warning to the UK over Ukraine drones — maps onto the move.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index sits near its high, reached on Aug 14 after a run up from June. The month's German news has been legal and security rather than corporate: a second Nord Stream suspect arrested in Croatia, seven suspects held over a banking hack, and Kallas pressing an EU sanctions package on Russia she says has already cost over €1 trillion.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index sits near the top of its two-month range, having climbed from its June low, with little in the week's news touching the listed sector directly. The domestic stories out of Paris were regulatory and institutional rather than corporate: the constitutional court struck down the under-15 social media ban, and cold calls now require consent first.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index has climbed to 1108, roughly 5% higher across the window, with the peak of 1120 on 13 August and no single Dutch event in view to explain the run. The daily move is flat, down 0.145%.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index has climbed roughly nine percent across the window, reaching its high of 20,210 on Aug 11 before easing to 20,060. The material here does not explain the move: the Spanish news in the window is an earthquake in Granada, the decision to extend the country's largest nuclear plant, and the Aug 12 total eclipse.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range, having climbed about 5% from its late-May low of 49,580 to a high of 53,720 on Aug 7 and holding close to that since. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index rose 7.39% over the period, climbing from 13,220 on Jun 3 to a high of 14,630 on Aug 10, and sits at 14,530. No reporting in this window explains the move.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up 5.7% over the window and 1% on the day, after a high of 3327 on Aug 5. The available material does not explain the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index has given up roughly 9% across the past 64 days. It peaked at 4463 on May 25, fell to a low of 3966 on Jun 29, and has traded close to that floor since, ending at 4059 after a slight rise on the day. The available material does not explain the decline.

xag.standing: A token backed by physical silver and priced per ounce, so it tracks the metal rather than a miner. Silver is both a monetary store and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics, brazing — which makes it more volatile than gold.
xag.recent: The price ran from a low of 29.80 on Aug 6 to a high of 67.31 on Aug 20, then gave back most of that gain to sit at 45.82, a net fall of 21.88% across the 31-day window.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its next meeting. It is a price, not a forecast: what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as the case for a cut or a hike is made or unmade.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract climbed from 39% on Aug 1 to a 75% peak on Aug 15 and sits at 68%, as the hold case hardened rather than the cut case. Fed minutes released on Aug 19 showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and traders through mid-August were already looking past CPI to the Fed's next tests.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US–Iran ceasefire holds to a set date. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for the ceasefire surviving — a running read on how close the two sides are to shooting again.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The price climbed from 83 on Aug 19 to 96 as Washington moved the confrontation onto financial ground: Treasury Secretary Bessent named the campaign "Economic Outcast" and designated nearly 60 entities, sanctions rather than strikes. Iran and Oman then agreed a temporary corridor through Hormuz, even as Rezaei threatened a shutdown.

wiki-lebanon.standing: Wikipedia's article on Lebanon, and the number of people who open it each day. Readership climbs when the country is at war, in political crisis or in the middle of a reconstruction fight, so the curve is a rough gauge of how much of the world is looking at it.
wiki-lebanon.recent: The peak on 21 August fell between two stories out of Beirut: families of journalists killed in Israeli strikes — 28 since 2023 — pressing the ICC to take a case it has no jurisdiction over, and Lebanon's finding that glyphosate in the soil of the southern border villages ran to 50 times normal levels.

wiki-petroleum.standing: Crude oil and the fuels refined from it — the base input for transport, freight, fertiliser and much of the chemicals industry. Its price and the politics around who pumps, refines and taxes it reach almost every household through what things cost to move.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Attention tracked a fuel-politics run rather than a price. Jamaat-e-Islami emir Rehman said patience had run out and threatened a shutdown over Pakistan's petroleum levy, after diesel rose Rs6.47 to Rs390.42 a litre and a crude line burst under homes in Karachi. Putin conceded not all fuel issues have been resolved.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States launches a military invasion of Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each turn between confrontation and negotiation.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The odds fell from 26 on Aug 2 to 16 as Washington chose money over missiles: Treasury Secretary Bessent named a sanctions campaign "Economic Outcast," designating nearly 60 entities and binding third countries. Iran and Oman then agreed a temporary corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump called Munir before his Tehran trip.

wiki-syria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Syria — a country whose government, borders and armed forces have all changed hands in living memory, and whose article people open when something there breaks.
wiki-syria.recent: The rise tracked the reckoning with the Assad era and the strikes around it: on 18 August a Syrian court sentenced Wassim al-Assad to death, Syria granted the IAEA access to an undeclared Assad-era nuclear site, and eight strikes hit an airbase in Idlib. Washington then delisted Syria on 24 August, and the SDF dissolved into the national army.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The English Wikipedia article on the 45th and 47th President of the United States. Its daily readership is one of the steadiest proxies for how much of the world is looking at Washington on any given day.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The month's traffic tracked a run of Trump decisions abroad: Kushner's meetings with Hamas and then Netanyahu to push a Gaza plan, the delisting of Syria after 47 years on the terror list, and a widened sanctions push on Iran that Gulf states have not welcomed. At home, the Supreme Court denied his appeal in the Carroll case without comment.

poly-will-renan-santos-win-the-2026-braz.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Renan Santos becomes Brazil's next president, priced in cents on the dollar. The number is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on candidacy news, party manoeuvring and polling rather than on votes cast.
poly-will-renan-santos-win-the-2026-braz.recent: The contract has drifted down through August, from 10% on 28 July to 3% on 23 August, with nothing in the month's news to arrest the slide. Polymarket itself made more headlines than this market did: JPMorgan cut the venue off on 14 August while still courting it.

wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.standing: The daily readership of the Wikipedia biography of Ukraine's president, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking him up rather than a measure of anything he does.
wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.recent: The late-July peak sat well above the月 rest of the month, and readership has fallen by roughly a third since. The mid-August low broke when anti-corruption agents searched Zelenskyy's own office on 19 August over a $3.4-million fraud probe, and again as Kyiv's allies convened on 24 August, where he said Patriot deliveries have halved since 2023.

stocks:XIACY.standing: A Chinese consumer-electronics maker turned carmaker: phones, home appliances and, since 2024, electric vehicles. Its shares are a read on Chinese consumer demand and on how far a hardware assembler can move up into its own silicon.
stocks:XIACY.recent: Xiaomi's Xring O3 chip, unveiled on 24 August, is an in-house AI mobile processor that challenges Qualcomm directly — a bid for design sovereignty rather than fabrication. The stock has drifted lower over the window, from $20.17 on Jul 29 to a $16.19 low on Aug 18, and the launch has not reversed it.
